selection_reasoning: These four tasks form a coherent multi-hop exploration and interaction sequence. The beacon is the culminating find because it's a rare, visually distinctive block that in our scene design can be placed in a structure requiring the player to navigate past other landmarks. The dependency chain works as follows: (1) 'find melon' serves as an initial orientation task - melons are placed near spawn to guide the player in the right direction. (2) 'find glass' requires the player to continue past the melons toward a glass-windowed structure. (3) 'mine jukebox' is inside or near that glass structure, requiring the player to have located the glass area first. (4) 'find beacon' is the final goal - the beacon is placed behind/above the jukebox area, and its beam is visible through the glass, but reaching it requires having navigated through the previous areas. This creates a logical spatial progression where each discovery leads to the next.

East wall opening at (14,1-3,5) lets player exit toward beacon. Jukebox at (11,1,5) inside building. Beacon at (17,3,5) on iron pyramid behind building. Diamond pickaxe provided for mining jukebox. Glass roof allows beacon beam visibility.
